MUJAHID:v1p140/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p140/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p140/r1.claim: Mujahid says those who hoarded what they withheld will be made to bring it on Resurrection Day.

MUQATIL:3:180/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:180/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:180/r1.claim: The verse addresses Jews who hoarded God's provision and withheld zakat; their treasure becomes a bald-headed male snake that coils around and bites them until judgment.

MUQATIL:3:180/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:180/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:180/r2.claim: God inherits the heavens and earth: their people perish while God remains; he knows their failure to give charity.

MAJAZ:v1p109/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p109/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p109/r3.claim: Khayran is accusative while huwa does not govern it: the clause is incomplete without its predicate.

MAJAZ:v1p109/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p109/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p109/r4.claim: Raising khayrun is possible in a completed clause such as mā ẓanantu Zaydan huwa khayrun minka; accusative is also permitted here.

MAJAZ:v1p109/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p109/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p109/r5.claim: Sayuṭawwaqūna means they will be made to wear or bear it around their necks.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p140/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p140/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p140/r2.claim: Those who withheld God's bounty will have what they withheld placed around their necks on Resurrection Day.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r1.claim: Ibrahim says the miser's hoarded wealth becomes a collar of fire.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p141/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the wealth appears as a snake that pecks its owner's head, identifies itself as the wealth he withheld, and coils around his neck.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r1.claim: The sin of withholding wealth will be fastened around their necks on Resurrection Day.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p116#5/r2.claim: One explanation says the person who withheld zakat will come with a bald snake around his neck, saying, “I am the zakat.”

TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r1.claim: Readers differ between the third-person reading yaḥsabanna and the second-person taḥsabanna.

TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r2.claim: Kufan grammarians understand the omitted object as stinginess itself: the misers must not think their miserliness good for them.

TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r3.claim: Basran grammarians say البخل is omitted after يحسبن; the pronoun and خير لهم supply clues to the missing nouns, as in the ellipsis at 57:10.

TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r4.speaker: بعض من أنكر قول من ذكرنا قوله من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v6p266#2/r4.claim: A critic of the Basran account reads من in 57:10 collectively and argues that the wording there is complete, while 3:180 has an ellipsis signaled by its two pronouns.

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r1.claim: Arabic usage can substitute “the foolish person” for “foolishness”; by analogy, “those who are miserly” can stand for the omitted “miserliness.”

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the second-person reading (ولا تحسبن); it supplies the subject of يحسبن, while “it is better for them” supplies its predicate, with miserliness understood.

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r3.claim: The first-person-plural? No: the third-person reading is not wrong, but it is less eloquent and less common in Arabic.

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r4.claim: The verse condemns people who withhold from their worldly wealth the zakat God made obligatory, since they wrongly think that miserliness benefits them in the Hereafter.

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r5.claim: Al-Suddi identifies them as people given wealth who refused to spend it in God’s path and did not pay its zakat.

TAB-FULL:v6p268/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p268/r6.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the misers as Jews who concealed the Torah’s account and description of Muhammad.

TAB-FULL:v6p271/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns the People of the Book, who withheld scripture instead of explaining it to people.

TAB-FULL:v6p271/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r2.claim: Mujahid likewise identifies the misers as Jews and connects the passage through the mention of the clear Book.

TAB-FULL:v6p271/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p271/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the interpretation that they withheld zakat: Prophetic reports say the one who withholds God’s due will wear it as a serpent, and the next verse describes Jews calling God poor when ordered to give.

TAB-FULL:v6p272/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r1.speaker: أبو مالك العبدي
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r1.claim: Abu Malik says a person who refuses a needy relative from his surplus will have that withheld wealth brought forth as a bald serpent.

TAB-FULL:v6p272/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r2.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet says a refused relative’s claim to surplus wealth will become a Hell-serpent that licks its lips and collars the refuser.

TAB-FULL:v6p272/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r3.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r3.claim: Abu Qaz‘ah reports the Prophet’s warning that a refusing relative will face a fiery serpent that licks its lips and collars him; the Prophet recited this verse.

TAB-FULL:v6p272/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r4.speaker: بهز بن حكيم
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r4.claim: Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father and grandfather, reports that a man who refuses his dependent’s request for surplus wealth will face a serpent on Judgment Day.

TAB-FULL:v6p272/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v6p272/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says the withheld wealth becomes a snake that pecks its owner’s head and says, “I am the wealth you withheld.”

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r1.claim: Ibn Masud describes the withheld wealth as a serpent twisting around its owner’s head; another transmission calls it a black serpent.

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the wealth will become a snake that pecks its owner’s head, identifies itself as his wealth, and coils around his neck.

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r3.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says anyone who fails to pay zakat will be represented by a bald serpent that collars him; he recited the verse.

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the wealth becomes a bald serpent that takes its owner by the neck and follows him until it casts him into the Fire.

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r5.speaker: أبو وائل
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r5.claim: Abu Wa'il explains the warning as withholding relatives’ due from one’s wealth; it becomes a snake around the neck that says, “I am your wealth.”

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r6.speaker: مسروق
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r6.claim: Masruq asked Ibn Masud about the verse and was told that a bald serpent will collar the miser and bite his head.

TAB-FULL:v6p274/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p274/r7.claim: Another interpretation says the withheld wealth will instead become a collar of fire around the misers’ necks.

TAB-FULL:v6p275/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r1.claim: Ibrahim interprets the punishment as a collar of fire, as reported through several transmissions.

TAB-FULL:v6p275/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas applies the verse to Jewish scholars who concealed Muhammad’s prophethood and urged others to conceal it.

TAB-FULL:v6p275/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r3.claim: Mujahid says those who concealed scripture will be compelled to produce on Judgment Day what they withheld in this life.

TAB-FULL:v6p275/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p275/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the serpent interpretation because of the Prophetic reports he cited, noting that no one knows God’s intended meaning better than the Prophet.

TAB-FULL:v6p276/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p276/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p276/r1.claim: God is everlasting after all creation perishes. Calling the heavens and earth His inheritance tells people that every creature’s property passes from them at death, and only God remains to own it.

TAB-FULL:v6p276/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p276/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p276/r2.claim: The miser’s punishment comes after death, when ownership has vanished; God knows all creatures’ deeds and repays each according to merit.

ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r3.claim: The verse is said to concern Jewish scholars who withheld knowledge of the Prophet’s status and opposed him; another view says it concerns those who withhold wealth and zakat.

ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r4.claim: In the construction, huwa is a separator (faṣl), called ʿimād by Kufans; Sibawayh allows it with verbs requiring a subject and predicate but does not discuss it between a nominal subject and predicate.

ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p492/r5.claim: He favors the yāʾ reading yaḥsabanna with an implicit subject; the tāʾ reading is also possible, with ‘miserliness’ omitted but indicated by the verb, as in ‘ask the town’ meaning its people.

ZAJJAJ:v1p493/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p493/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p493/r1.claim: God’s inheritance of heaven and earth means He makes their inhabitants self-sufficient while retaining all they contain; the analogy speaks in terms people understand, since inheritance normally returns owned property.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p220/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p220/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p220/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read والله بما يعملون with yāʾ; the others use tāʾ.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the miserly people include the People of Scripture, who withheld the Book from explaining it to others.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r2.claim: Hasan says they will be punished for what they withheld; they include disbelievers and hypocrites who refuse to spend in God's path.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says they withhold wealth from spending in God's path and fail to pay its alms.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r4.claim: The Prophet says a man who fails to pay alms will have his wealth transformed into a bald snake that collars him, then recites this verse as confirmation.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r5.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says the withheld wealth becomes a snake that bites its owner's head and says it is the wealth he hoarded.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r6.speaker: شعبة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r6.claim: Shuba's similar transmission describes a black snake coiling around the miser's head.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r7.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p826/r7.claim: Another Ibn Masud report says a bald snake with two fangs bites the head and tells the miser it is his withheld wealth.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r1.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r1.claim: Masruq reports Ibn Masud's description of a bald snake collaring the miser and biting his temples.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r2.claim: Mujahid says misers will be made to bring what they withheld.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r3.claim: Ibrahim says they will be collared with a collar of fire.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r4.speaker: جبريل
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas quotes Gabriel saying that God owns all creatures, the heavens, the earth, and everything between them.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains God's knowledge of people's deeds, as far as this page records it.

IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p827/r6.claim: Qatada glosses خبير as fully aware of His creation.

NAHHAS:v1p420/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p420/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p420/r3.claim: On Nafi's reading, الذين is nominative with first object omitted; البخل is intended, and هو is an emphatic or separating pronoun.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r1.claim: They read ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون with yāʾ and kasra on sīn; across the cited verses their third-person readings keep the named group as the subject.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r2.claim: Nafi and Ibn Amir use yāʾ for the first clauses, but tāʾ for فلا تحسبنهم; Nafi has kasra and Ibn Amir fatḥa on sīn in that final form.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r3.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r3.claim: Hamza reads the cited clauses about disbelievers and those who rejoice with tāʾ, opening both bāʾ and sīn; the form addresses the Prophet directly.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r4.speaker: عاصم والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r4.claim: Asim and al-Kisai read most forms in the sura with tāʾ, but use yāʾ in the clauses about hoarders and disbelievers; they differ in the vowel of sīn.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p100/r5.claim: With yāʾ, الذين is the subject and the clause that follows can fill both objects of حسب; ما can mean 'that which' or function as a verbal noun.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r1.claim: In ولا يحسبن الذين يبخلون, the hoarders are the subject, the first object (البخل) is omitted but understood, and هو separates it from خيرًا لهم.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p103/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan dislikes the yāʾ reading for the next clauses because حسب is left without an expressed object, although it often takes two.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r1.claim: They read والله بما يعملون خبير with yāʾ, continuing the third-person reference to those who hoard; God knows their withholding of due rights and requites it.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r2.speaker: باقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r2.claim: The other readers use tāʾ, linking the clause to the preceding address وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا and referring to the believers' righteous work.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r3.claim: Ibn Amir alone repeats bāʾ in بالبينات وبالزبر, as in Syrian codices; the other readers omit the second bāʾ because conjunction already carries the preposition.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p113/r4.claim: Repeating bāʾ is valid for emphasis, as repeated nouns appear in poetry; both the repeated-preposition and shared-preposition constructions are sound Arabic.

SULAMI:v1p128#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p128#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p128#2/r1.claim: The path calls for generosity and against miserliness: give wealth, self, secret, spirit, and everything; withholding anything for God veils a person, while looking to anything besides Him deprives one of nearness. A report says God's friend is formed for generosity.

SULAMI:v1p128#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p128#2/r2.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p128#2/r2.claim: A prophetic report says that God's friend is formed with a disposition toward generosity.

THALABI:v3p218/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p218/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p218/r8.claim: For the yā' reading of يحسبن, هو is the subject and the predicate is خير; the implied object is that stinginess, elided after يبخلون just as arrival can be elided after a verb of coming.

THALABI:v3p219/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p219/r1.claim: A cited poetic line illustrates the implied noun after a verb, and similar constructions occur in the verses about God's true message and what the learned recognize as truth.

THALABI:v3p219/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p219/r2.claim: The tā' reading is analyzed as repetition or apposition, as in the earlier verse about delayed respite; هو شر لهم means that stinginess is evil for them.

THALABI:v3p219/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r3.speaker: المبرد
THALABI:v3p219/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the future particle س in سيطوقون is a threat, with the sense 'they will be made to wear it.'

THALABI:v3p219/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبو وائل وابن مالك وابن فرعة والشعبي والسدي
THALABI:v3p219/r4.claim: They interpret the withheld wealth or unpaid zakat as a serpent that coils around its owner at resurrection, humiliates him, and leads him to Hell; a Prophetic report supports this.

THALABI:v3p219/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r5.speaker: أبو وائل
THALABI:v3p219/r5.claim: Abu Wail reports from Abdullah that a man who withholds zakat will have a shuja' serpent placed around his neck at resurrection; the Prophet recited this verse as proof.

THALABI:v3p219/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r6.speaker: رجل من بني قيس
THALABI:v3p219/r6.claim: A man of Banu Qays reports that withholding from a needy relative brings a snake from Hell which coils around the miser, and the Prophet recited the verse.

THALABI:v3p219/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p219/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v3p219/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that withheld property becomes a foul bald serpent which identifies itself as the owner's wealth, coils around him, and accompanies him to Hell.

THALABI:v3p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
THALABI:v3p220/r1.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says the miser is made to wear a collar of fire around his neck at resurrection.

THALABI:v3p220/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p220/r10.claim: On the knowledge interpretation, being collared means carrying the burden and sin of what was withheld; God's inheritance of heaven and earth means He remains after creatures and their possessions pass away.

THALABI:v3p220/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v3p220/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets the verse as requiring misers to produce on Judgment Day the wealth they withheld in this life.

THALABI:v3p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r3.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v3p220/r3.claim: Al-Mu'arrikh says people are bound to their deeds as a collar is bound to the neck, citing the expression for making someone wear his deed like a dove's collar.

THALABI:v3p220/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v3p220/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet said that one who withholds zakat will be in the Fire at resurrection.

THALABI:v3p220/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r5.speaker: هشام بن عروة
THALABI:v3p220/r5.claim: Hisham ibn Urwa reports from his father that charity does not mix with property without destroying it.

THALABI:v3p220/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r6.speaker: أبو بريدة
THALABI:v3p220/r6.claim: A report from Abu Burayda's father says that when a people withhold zakat, God withholds rain from them.

THALABI:v3p220/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
THALABI:v3p220/r7.claim: Hasan tells of a sheep owner whose meager charity was protected by a large ram in a dream; afterward he increased that animal's descendants in his giving.

THALABI:v3p220/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r8.speaker: الثعلبي
THALABI:v3p220/r8.claim: Al-Tha'labi cites a poem asking how long a miser expects to live with his wealth, noting that the dead take none of it and someone else inherits it.

THALABI:v3p220/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p220/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p220/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse concerns Jewish scholars who concealed Muhammad's description; their stinginess was withholding revealed knowledge, as in the verse about hiding God's bounty.

THALABI:v3p221/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p221/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p221/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the final verb with yā'—God knows what they do—while the other readers address the listeners with tā'.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r4.claim: Wahidi foregrounds the majority exegetical view that the warning concerns those who withhold zakat.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p132/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās offers an alternative: the verse concerns Jewish rabbis who hid Muhammad’s description and prophethood, with miserliness meaning concealment of knowledge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r1.claim: The verse is read with either ya or ta; with ya, the withholding people are the subject and an omitted first object is inferred as withholding from the verb.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r2.claim: The omitted object is bukhl: the meaning is not to suppose that withholding is good, as in saying that lying is bad or the poem's unstated pursuit is kingship.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r3.claim: هو is a separative particle, called ʿimād by Kufans; it clarifies the predicate after the implied verbal noun bukhl.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r4.claim: For the ta-reading, al-Zajjaj understands the object as the withholding of those who withhold, with the annexed noun omitted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p215/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ataa's narration, Ibn Masud, al-Shaʿbi, al-Suddi, and most exegetes say the verse was revealed about those withholding obligatory zakat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the wealth subject to withholding includes gold, silver, livestock, and crops—the kinds on which zakat is due.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains that withholding is evil because it earns them God's punishment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r3.claim: Most exegetes say the withheld wealth becomes a snake worn around the miser's neck on Judgment Day and bites from head to foot.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet said one who fails to pay zakat will have a large snake placed around his neck, then recited this verse as confirmation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r5.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi interprets the punishment as a collar of fire around their necks.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r6.speaker: المؤرج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r6.claim: Al-Muʾarrij reads the collar figuratively as being bound to one's deeds; Arabic uses taṭwīq for obligation, and 2:184's yutīqūnahu means undertaking it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p218/r7.claim: On the figurative reading, Ibn al-Anbari says they bear the recompense of what they withheld; the collar is a metaphor for compulsion, not a literal collar.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas in al-Awfi's report says the verse concerns Jews concealing Muhammad's description; their bukhl is withholding knowledge God gave them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r2.claim: This reading is supported by 4:37, which speaks of miserliness and concealing God's bounty; the collar then means bearing the sin of concealed knowledge.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r3.speaker: ابن كيسان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r3.claim: Ibn Kaysan and Abu Ishaq prefer the interpretation that those concealing knowledge carry its sin.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r4.claim: All commentators say God inherits the heavens and earth because their inhabitants and possessions perish, leaving God as their sole owner.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says inheritance language addresses what people understand: the claimed ownership of all owners ends, leaving God's ownership alone.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari notes that Arabs say one person inherits another's knowledge when he becomes its sole possessor after sharing it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p221/r7.claim: Solomon's inheritance of David in 27:16 can mean inheriting his knowledge after David had shared or predominated in it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r1.claim: The ya-reading of يعملون matches the preceding third-person wording about being collared and God's knowledge of what they do.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r2.claim: The ta-reading matches the address in 3:179, 'if you believe and fear God'; either reading frames God's knowledge as grounds for recompense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v6p223/r3.claim: The author says the third-person reading is contextually closer than the direct address.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r1.claim: The warning was revealed about people who withheld zakat.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r2.claim: They think withholding God's bounty is good, but it is evil because they thereby deserve God's punishment.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r3.claim: On Judgment Day the hoarded money becomes a snake that collars its owner and bites him from head to foot.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:180-181/r4.claim: God inherits the heavens and earth because he outlives their owners and alone remains owner of their property and wealth.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r1.claim: They read the four occurrences of the prohibition with yāʾ, including the forms about disbelievers, misers, and those who rejoice; the final occurrence has a ḍamma on its bāʾ.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وابن عامر ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r2.claim: They use yāʾ in the occurrences except فلا تحسبنهم, which they read with tāʾ.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r3.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r3.claim: Hamza reads all four forms with tāʾ, addressing the listener.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r4.speaker: عاصم والكسائي وخلف
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r4.claim: They read the first two occurrences with yāʾ and the remaining occurrences with tāʾ.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r5.claim: The tāʾ reading repeats the address in meaning, as though the Prophet, hearer, or human being were told not to suppose; الذين is accusative.

JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1398#2/r6.claim: With yāʾ, الذين is nominative as the subject of the verb, with an implied meaning: let the disbeliever not count Our reprieve of them as good.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Jewish scholars who concealed Muhammad's description and prophethood; their miserliness is concealing knowledge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r2.claim: Being made to wear what they withheld means bearing its burden and sin, like those who carry their loads on their backs.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r3.claim: God inherits the heavens and earth because He remains after creatures die and their possessions vanish, as another verse says He inherits the earth and everyone on it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142#2/r4.claim: Basra and Mecca readers use the third-person 'they do'; the remaining readers address the audience directly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r1.claim: Miserly people should not think their withholding is good; what they withhold will become a creature encircling and biting them on Judgment Day, as Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Wail, al-Shabi, and al-Suddi say.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's image of unpaid zakat becoming a bald snake with two marks that coils around its owner, bites his cheeks, and says, 'I am your wealth, your treasure.'

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r3.claim: Abu Dharr reports that unpaid rights on camels, cattle, or sheep make the animals trample and gore their owner on Judgment Day, repeatedly returning until judgment is complete.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r4.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai says the withheld property will become a collar of fire around their necks.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p142/r5.claim: Mujahid says they will be ordered on Judgment Day to bring the property they withheld in this world.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r1.claim: God owns what the heavens and earth contain and what their inhabitants inherit; hoarding His property rather than spending it in His cause is irrational.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r2.claim: The argument parallels the command to spend from what God made people stewards over.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474#2/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading shifts to direct address and heightens the threat; the yāʾ reading follows the preceding third-person form.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r1.claim: The tāʾ reading supplies an omitted noun, ‘the miserliness of those who are miserly’; with yāʾ, the subject may be the Messenger or another person, or the misers themselves with an omitted first object.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r2.claim: The omitted object is licensed by the nearby verb يبخلون; هو is a separator pronoun, and al-Aʿmash omitted it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r3.claim: Being ‘collared’ explains the evil of miserliness as bearing its consequence like a collar; an Arabic proverb uses the image for disgrace.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r4.claim: A report says withheld zakat becomes a snake around the miser's neck, biting and speaking; the Prophet describes a hairless snake, with another report specifying a black one.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r5.claim: The Prophet says the one who withholds zakat will be collared by a hairless serpent; another transmitted wording says a black serpent.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r6.speaker: النخعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p474/r6.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi interprets the collar as a collar of fire.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r1.speaker: السدي وجماعة من المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r1.claim: They say the verse condemns withholding wealth from God's path, including failure to give obligatory zakat.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says a relative denied a kinsman the surplus he requested, and a bald snake will emerge at Resurrection, lick its lips, and coil around him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r3.claim: Many sound reports address withholding zakat and hoarding wealth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد وجماعة من أهل التفسير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r4.claim: They say the verse concerns People of the Book withholding what they knew about Muhammad.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r5.claim: On the latter interpretation, yutawwaqūn means they will bear the consequence of what they withheld, from the root for capacity rather than literally being collared.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r6.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r6.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai says they will be given a collar of fire at Resurrection, consistent with the wealth interpretation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r7.claim: Mujahid says they will be charged to produce the like of what they withheld, fitting the interpretation about withheld knowledge.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r8.claim: With yaḥsabanna read in the third person, alladhīna yabkhalūn is the subject; an omitted first object is 'their stinginess,' khayran is the second object, and huwa is a separator.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p546#3/r9.claim: The understood noun 'stinginess' is supplied by the verb 'they are stingy,' like the poet's use of 'foolish' to imply foolishness.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r1.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r1.claim: The verse cited in the wāfir meter shows how an adjective such as 'foolish' implies the abstract quality of folly.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r2.claim: With taḥsabanna addressed to Muhammad, an omitted genitive is understood: do not consider the stinginess of those who are stingy good for them; it is like 'ask the town.'

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r3.claim: Calling the heavens and earth God's inheritance speaks in human terms of everything perishing and God alone remaining its owner, though His ownership is eternal.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r4.speaker: ابن كثير، أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r4.claim: They read 'God knows what they do' with third-person yāʾ, referring to those who are stingy and collared.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p547/r5.claim: The other readers use second-person tāʾ, shifting from absent to addressed listeners after the preceding address in 3:179.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:3:180#2/r1.claim: The Prophet is also reported to describe a relative who withholds God's bounty: God will bring a serpent from Hell, which will lick its tongue and encircle the miser.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r2.speaker: النخعي
TABRISI:3:180#2/r2.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī interprets the punishment as a collar of fire around the miser's neck on Judgment Day.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:3:180#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the miser will be made to produce on Judgment Day the wealth he withheld.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:3:180#2/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī reads the punishment as the withheld wealth becoming a collar used to torment its owner, like the heated treasure in 9:35.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسلم
TABRISI:3:180#2/r5.claim: Ibn Muslim says the harm returns on the miser and becomes a collar, as in the image of each person's deed fastened to his neck in 17:13; Arabs can use neck or throat for the whole body.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:3:180#2/r6.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās takes the verse to concern those who concealed the description of Muhammad, with God's bounty referring to the Torah containing that description; the first view better fits the context.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:180#2/r7.claim: God inheriting heaven and earth means all creatures die and every owner's property ends while God's ownership remains forever; this urges people not to cling to wealth that will pass away.

TABRISI:3:180#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180#2/r8.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:3:180#2/r8.claim: The verse connects to the prior discussion because, like their stinginess about jihad, they were stingy about spending and zakat; another view says they concealed Muhammad's prophethood.

TABRISI:3:180/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:180/r1.claim: With the yāʾ reading, those who withhold are the subject and the understood first object is their withholding; huwa separates the subject from the predicate. The tāʾ reading addresses the Prophet and omits the object meaning their withholding.

TABRISI:3:180/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:180/r2.claim: Bukhul is withholding what is due; its lexical root also connotes difficulty in giving.

TABRISI:3:180/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
TABRISI:3:180/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb read the end of the verse with yāʾ, referring to those who withhold; the other readers address the audience with tāʾ.

TABRISI:3:180/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:180/r4.claim: The rebuke concerns people who withhold the obligatory rights from wealth God has given them; such stinginess is bad for them, not good as they suppose.

TABRISI:3:180/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:3:180/r5.claim: One interpretation says withheld wealth will become a collar around its owner's neck; the verse concerns zakat refusers, as reported from Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, al-Shaʿbī, and others.

TABRISI:3:180/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:180/r6.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:3:180/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that a man who fails to pay zakat will have a serpent placed around his neck on Judgment Day, then recites the verse.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبو هريرة وابن عباس عن أبي صالح والشعبي ومجاهد والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r1.claim: One occasion identifies people who withhold the required alms from their wealth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r2.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس وابن جريج عن مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r2.claim: Another occasion identifies Jewish scholars who concealed the Prophet's description and prophethood; al-Zajjaj prefers this view.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r3.claim: He prefers the interpretation about scholars concealing the Prophet's attributes and prophethood.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r4.claim: The grammar omits the verbal noun “stinginess”: “those who are miserly” means “do not think their stinginess good for them.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p512/r5.claim: What God granted means wealth under the alms interpretation, and knowledge under the interpretation about concealing the Prophet's description.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r1.claim: The pronoun “it” refers to the implied noun stinginess, understood from “they are miserly.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r2.claim: The withheld wealth will appear as a bald serpent that follows its owner and coils around his neck, according to a hadith from the Prophet reported by Ibn Masud.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r3.speaker: منصور عن مجاهد وإبراهيم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r3.claim: The withheld wealth will be made into a collar of fire.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r4.speaker: ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r4.claim: To be collared with it means being made responsible for bringing it back.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r5.claim: The sin of their miserliness will bind their necks.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r6.claim: The heavens' and earth's inheritance means that their inhabitants die while the Lord of the worlds remains.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r7.claim: The address uses a familiar idea: people call property that returns to a person after another owner's death an inheritance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p513/r8.claim: Inheritance here means God alone possesses what no one else possessed after all creation dies.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r1.claim: The passage shifts from urging self-sacrifice in jihad to urging financial sacrifice and warning those who withhold wealth in God's cause.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r2.claim: For Hamza's second-person reading, the construction means do not consider the stinginess of the stingy good for them; a noun for stinginess is elided because the verb supplies it.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r3.claim: With the other readers' third-person form, the subject may be the Prophet or anyone in general, or the stingy themselves with the object their stinginess omitted.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r4.claim: The omitted object is licensed by context, as in the saying about lying being bad and the phrase about a fool running toward folly; al-Farra's verse uses به for kingship, inferable from kings.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r5.claim: Basrans call هو a separating pronoun and Kufans a support; it marks the added relation in which the subject is predicated of the predicate.

RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p91#2/r6.claim: The condemned stinginess can concern any good or benefit, including either wealth or knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r1.speaker: أكثر العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r1.claim: Most scholars define stinginess as withholding what is obligatory, not declining voluntary giving: the severe threat and blame fit neglected duties, not optional generosity.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r2.claim: Other proofs include that God cannot give without limit, so refusing any extra favor cannot make Him stingy; a hadith calls stinginess a dreadful disease, and withholding voluntary gifts would not warrant that label.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r3.claim: If every refusal of a voluntary gift were stinginess, even the owner of all wealth could escape the charge only by giving everything; 2:3 praises spending only part of God's provision and 2:5 calls such people guided and successful.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92#2/r4.claim: Obligatory spending includes one's own needs and dependents, zakat, defense when Muslims face an attack on lives or property, and enough aid to keep a desperate person alive; withholding these is stinginess.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r1.claim: One view applies the warning to withholding wealth: the withheld money will become punishment, while the money itself will not remain with them because God inherits all.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r2.claim: A second view applies it to withholding knowledge: Jews concealed Muhammad's description and the glad tidings of his coming in the Torah and Gospel, although knowledge is God's gift.

RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p92/r3.claim: Razi prefers wealth: the collar threat fits money literally, whereas knowledge requires metaphor; reading wealth also continues the preceding exhortation to spend in jihad, unlike the knowledge reading.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r1.claim: If stinginess means concealing knowledge, the collar is a fiery bridle on the mouths and tongues that failed to speak the truth; a prophetic report threatens such a bridle for concealing known knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r2.claim: The knowledge interpretation is plausible because the Quran also condemns Jewish stinginess, and the next verse cites a Jewish statement; the warning may cover withholding both knowledge and wealth.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r3.claim: The Mu'tazilites cite the verse as a decisive threat against grave sinners: it promises loss of reward and fire and explicitly says the withheld thing will be collared at resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p93#2/r4.claim: God's inheritance means either all that the inhabitants of heaven and earth own, making their withholding from Him pointless, or, according to most, God's sole ownership after all creatures die; Razi reports Ibn al-Anbari's linguistic point that inheritance can mean exclusive possession after sharing, as in Solomon's inheritance of David.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r1.claim: A literal interpretation makes the withheld wealth a tormenting collar: it may become snakes around the neck and body, or a collar of fire; the neck image fits unpaid zakat, and the body image fits hoarded property.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says withheld zakat will become a two-spotted serpent collar that bites the miser's cheeks and says it is the zakat he withheld in worldly life.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the collar as being required at resurrection to produce what one withheld, when compliance is impossible, as a reproach for not giving it when able.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r4.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Abbas in 2:184 understands the duty as something they are burdened with but cannot bear, supporting Mujahid's interpretation of the impossible demand.

RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p93/r5.claim: A figurative reading says they will carry the sin of stinginess; Arabic represents an emphatically imposed burden as being placed around someone's neck, as in the statement about each person's deeds.

RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the final verb in the third person, referring to the misers whose denial of rights God knows and will punish; the other readers address the audience directly, continuing the preceding second-person address.

RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r2.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v9p94/r2.claim: Al-Kashshaf calls the third-person reading a rhetorical shift of address and says it intensifies the threat.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r1.claim: The Prophet says a miser who refuses a relative's request for surplus wealth will be brought on Judgment Day as a panting fire-serpent that collars him; no grading is stated.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and other scholars say the verse instead concerns the People of the Book concealing what they knew about Muhammad; on this reading, 'will be collared' means they will bear punishment, from the sense of capacity in 2:184.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i says they will be given a fiery collar on Judgment Day, an interpretation that fits the financial reading.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r4.claim: Another explanation is that people will be bound to their deeds as a neck is bound by a collar, paralleling 17:13; a poem by Abdullah ibn Jahsh to Abu Sufyan uses the image of burdening someone like a dove's collar.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r5.claim: Bukh is withholding a right that is due; refusing something not owed is not blameworthy. Hijaz and other Arabs differ in the verb's morphology.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r6.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r6.claim: Al-Nahhas notes that Hijaz speakers say yabkhalūna/bakhilū, while other Arabs use the other conjugation; Ibn Faris gives additional noun and verb forms.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#2/r7.claim: In a report cited by al-Mawardi, the Prophet asks the Ansar to name their leader; when they name the stingy Jad ibn Qays, he says no disease is worse than miserliness and tells a story of hosts avoiding guests until men and women become sexually occupied with their own sex.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r1.claim: Views differ on whether bukh and shuḥḥ are synonymous: bukh is withholding what one has, while shuḥḥ is eagerness to acquire what one lacks; another says shuḥḥ is greed, which the author prefers.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r2.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r2.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet warning against injustice and greed, which destroyed earlier peoples, led them to bloodshed, and made them violate sacred things; Muslim transmits it.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r3.claim: This report refutes the claim that shuḥḥ is only refusal of recommended charity: that would not merit such severe warnings and ruin in both worlds.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r4.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a Prophetic statement that fighting dust and Hell's smoke never meet in a Muslim's nostrils, nor do faith and greed coexist; al-Nasa'i transmits it.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r5.claim: The warning shows shuḥḥ is more blameworthy than bukh, although a report that a believer cannot be miserly suggests a degree of equivalence.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#3/r6.claim: God says He will inherit the heavens and earth: after creation and ownership disappear, He remains; human inheritance is only an analogy, since God already owned everything and human wealth was a loan returned to its owner.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180#4/r1.claim: The parallel in 19:40 teaches people to spend before death rather than leave their wealth as God's inheritance; only what they spent benefits them.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r1.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r1.claim: Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and al-Farra supply an omitted object: people should not suppose stinginess is good for them; the omission is signaled by the verb 'are stingy.'

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r2.claim: The omitted noun is illustrated by 'whoever is truthful, it is better for him,' where 'truth' is understood from 'truthful'; a poem similarly uses 'fool' to imply folly.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r3.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas calls Hamza's second-person reading very remote; it can be parsed as forbidding one to consider the stinginess of the stingy good, like 'ask the village.'

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r4.claim: The pronoun huwa is an emphatic separator for Basran grammarians and a supporting particle for Kufans; it can also be the subject of a nominal sentence meaning 'it is better for them.'

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r5.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the sīn in 'they will be collared' signals a threat: they will be made to wear it later.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r6.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Wa'il, Abu Malik, al-Suddi, al-Sha'bi, and others say the verse concerns withholding wealth, spending in God's path, and obligatory zakat; Abu Hurayra reports the zakat-evader transformed into a bald serpent that collars him and says, 'I am your wealth, your treasure.'

QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r7.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:3:180/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says anyone who withholds zakat will be made into a bald snake that collars him; the Prophet recites this verse as proof. Ibn Majah transmits it.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r1.claim: The readings vary in person and syntax; with a second-person reading, an omitted noun is supplied to make the two objects agree, while third-person readings can take either the Prophet or the stingy as subject.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r2.claim: Stinginess is evil because it brings punishment; on the day of resurrection its consequences will cling to the miser like a collar.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r3.claim: A prophetic report says that one who fails to pay zakat will have his wealth made into a serpent around his neck on the Day of Resurrection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r4.claim: God's inheritance of heaven and earth means either that all their contents belong to Him, so misers withhold His property, or that He inherits what they hoard after they die, leaving them regret and punishment.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:180/r5.claim: God knows both withholding and giving and will recompense them; Nafi, Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the address in the second person, intensifying the threat.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r1.claim: The t- and y-readings allow different implied subjects: on one parse bukhul is supplied, هو is a separator, and خير is the second object; with the y-reading the subject may be the Prophet or another person.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r2.claim: If the hoarders themselves are subject, the understood phrase is 'their miserliness'; هو remains a separator and خير the second object.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r3.claim: Miserliness is evil because wealth will leave them while its burden remains with them.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r4.claim: A hadith says a person withholding zakat will have the wealth made into a male bald snake with two fangs, placed around his neck to bite and drive him toward the Fire.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r5.claim: God inherits everything in the heavens and earth; the hoarders withhold what belongs to Him. Mawārith derives from mawārith with wāw changed to yāʾ after kasra.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r6.speaker: المكي وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p194#2/r6.claim: They read the closing verb with yāʾ; the t-reading is a rhetorical shift that intensifies the threat, while yāʾ follows the apparent subject.

QASHANI:3:179-180/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:179-180/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:179-180/r4.claim: Those who hoard God's gifts of wealth, knowledge, power, or self instead of giving them to the deserving, prophets, and saints will bear them as a collar causing deprivation, disgrace, and a veil from divine beauty.

QASHANI:3:179-180/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:179-180/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:179-180/r5.claim: Souls, powers, abilities, knowledge, wealth, and all that exists already belong to God as the inheritance of heaven and earth, so miserliness with them is senseless.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r2.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r2.claim: Al-Suddī and others say the verse concerns withholding wealth and spending in God's path.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās in a report from ʿAṭiyya, Mujāhid, Ibn Jurayj, and others, with al-Zajjāj's preference, say it concerns People of the Book withholding what they knew about Muhammad.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayra, another Ibn ʿAbbās narration, al-Shaʿbī, and Mujāhid applies it to people withholding obligatory zakāt; another view concerns family support.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r5.claim: The verse follows exhortation to sacrifice lives in jihad with exhortation to spend wealth in jihad and elsewhere; legal miserliness is withholding what is obligatory.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r6.claim: Ḥamza reads تحسبن with tāʾ, making الذين the first object after an understood possessive; the other readers use yāʾ and require a subject/object analysis, with an omitted first object if the misers are subject.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r7.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p450/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash omits هو, making خيرا the object of تحسبن; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says يبخلون signals the omitted noun بخلهم, though the author distinguishes this from the poetic example he cites.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r1.claim: The author offers an unusual coordination analysis: ما آتاهم is the first object sought by تحسبن while هو and خيرا are its second object; يبخلون governs the same phrase through a preposition, and the second verb is given precedence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r2.claim: Because negating that miserliness or the withheld gift is good leaves open neutrality or harm, the following clause explicitly establishes that it is harmful.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r3.claim: The collaring is apparently figurative: they will be bound to the punishment like someone forced to wear a collar, as expressed in an Arabic proverb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r4.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p451/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī begins a literal interpretation in which they will be given a collar on the Day of Resurrection; the passage continues in the next segment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r1.claim: Mujāhid and others take سيطوقون from الطاقة, meaning they will be made to bear the punishment of what they withheld; the author says this does not fit withholding knowledge about the Messenger.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r2.claim: Mujāhid also says they will be required to produce the like of what they withheld.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r3.speaker: أبو وائل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r3.claim: Abū Wāʾil describes a person who withholds relatives' rightful share of his wealth as being collared by a serpent that says, 'I am your wealth.'

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r4.claim: A prophetic hadith says a relative denied one's surplus wealth will come as a fiery serpent, licking its lips, and collar the miser; reports about withholding zakāt and hoarding are many and sound.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r5.claim: God's inheritance of the heavens and earth can mean He truly owns everything attributed to creatures, so people should not hoard what they only temporarily enjoy; the verse links this to 57:7.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase foretells the world's end: God inherits what creatures leave behind, language framed for human understanding although His ownership has always been complete.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p452/r7.claim: The closing description 'God is aware of what you do' threatens misers for their wrongdoing; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read the verb in the third person, while others address the misers directly, which the author calls the better reading of the shift.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r1.claim: The passage's rhetorical devices include specification, repetition, antithesis, metaphor, paronomasia, shifts of address, and ellipsis; its metaphors include rushing, buying, respite, sin-increase, and pure versus corrupt.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p453/r2.claim: The shift in والله بما تعملون خبير is an address shift for readers of تعملون with tāʾ; the shift in أنتم depends on whom the address is understood to target.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r1.claim: The cited poem continues Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s evidence that a participle can imply its verbal noun: السفيه signals السفه.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r2.claim: Al-Shaykh says the analogy fails: verbs signal their verbal nouns more strongly than participles, and the poem uses implication rather than the verse’s deletion.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r3.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ alternatively makes هو the first object, referring to the hoarded wealth signaled by يبخلون.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r4.claim: This fails because an object of يحسبن should be accusative إياه, with no need to posit a nominative pronoun replacing an accusative.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaykh proposes a competing-governance analysis: يحسبن seeks two objects and يبخلون a prepositional object, so the latter governs the shared phrase and the former’s first object is omitted.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r1.claim: The author notes a grammatical dispute about applying a later verb to a shared object: the Basran view deletes the earlier non-subject object, except an object of ظن, while another view challenges this restriction; the Kūfans allow the deletion.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r2.claim: The author questions the restriction: if one object can be deleted concisely outside verb competition, it may also be omitted when verbs compete; this strengthens al-Shaykh’s parse.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r3.claim: Makkī discusses the two readings; ميراث is a verbal noun like ميعاد, with yāʾ replacing wāw after kasra.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:3:180#3/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read يعملون in the third person, matching الذين يبخلون; others address the audience by shift or by returning to وإن تؤمنوا وتتقوا.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r1.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads يحسبن with direct address; الذين is first object and خيرا second, with omitted بخل to make the predicate fit.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls deletion of بخل weak because it precedes its evidence; the author replies that evidence may precede or follow an omission.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r3.claim: In Ḥamza’s reading هو separates the two objects, not emphasis; other parses fail because خيرا is accusative and the preceding noun is explicit though omitted analytically.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r4.claim: In the majority’s third-person reading, the subject may be the Messenger or any assessor, making الذين first object after deleting بخل, or the verb may be attributed to the hoarders.

SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:180/r5.claim: If the hoarders are the subject, the first object can be omitted because يبخلون signals it, as السفيه signals السفه in the cited poem.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r2.claim: A miser should not think hoarding God’s bounty benefits him; it harms his religion and may harm his worldly life too.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p173#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says one who withholds zakat will be made into a bald snake with two spots that coils around him and declares itself his wealth and treasure; al-Bukhari reports it uniquely by this route.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r1.speaker: النسائي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r1.claim: Al-Nasa'i considers the Ibn Umar route through Abdullah ibn Dinar more reliable than the Abu Hurayra route through his father and Abu Salih; Ibn Kathir says both may be correct.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that a person who withholds zakat is pursued by a bald snake, and recites this verse as its scriptural basis.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r3.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi grades the Ibn Masud report hasan sahih; al-Tabari also transmits it from Ibn Masud as a Companion statement.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r4.speaker: ثوبان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p174/r4.claim: A report from Thawban says an abandoned treasure appears as a bald snake that follows its owner and bites him; Ibn Kathir calls its chain strong and good though the collectors did not include it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175#2/r1.claim: Because God inherits the heavens and earth, people should spend from what He temporarily entrusted to them and send ahead what will benefit them in the afterlife; God knows their intentions.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r1.speaker: بهز بن حكيم عن أبيه عن جده
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r1.claim: The Prophet says someone who refuses his dependent the surplus of his wealth will face a snake licking the surplus he withheld.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r2.speaker: أبو قزعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r2.claim: A report says that a relative who withholds God’s surplus from a needy relative will face a snake from Hell; alternate transmissions make it a Companion report or a mursal report.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p175/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about People of the Book who withheld the revealed scriptures from explaining them; Ibn Kathir prefers the earlier context, though this meaning is included and may also fit especially well.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r1.claim: Hamza reads the warning as addressed to the Prophet; the other readers make those who withhold the grammatical subject.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r2.claim: The withheld wealth consists of religious dues from God's grace, not something its possessors earned through miserliness.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r3.claim: They wrongly suppose hoarding will grow their wealth; miserliness is harmful, and what they withheld will become a terrifying serpent encircling their necks and striking their faces on Judgment Day.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r4.claim: The Prophet said that one given wealth who fails to pay its zakat will have that wealth become a bald serpent with two black marks, which collars and seizes him, saying it is his wealth and hoard; he then recited this verse.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r5.claim: Since owners spend when they know wealth will pass to an heir, God explains that all wealth belongs to Him and that He will inherit the heavens and earth after reviving beings and ending their transient possessions.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r6.claim: Because the passage concerns hidden acts and unseen matters, ending with God's knowledge of people's deeds gives a forceful warning; the wording addresses the followers in most readings.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r7.claim: The address reading is more threatening than retaining the preceding third-person construction, and fronting the phrase about their deeds stresses God's knowledge beyond human comprehension.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p188/r8.claim: God's being informed encompasses every act of the heart, tongue, and limbs.

DURR-FULL:v2p393/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r10.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r10.claim: The warning applies to both an unbeliever and a believer who withhold spending for God's cause.

DURR-FULL:v2p393/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r11.claim: The Prophet says an owner who fails to pay zakat will be garroted by a bald snake that identifies itself as his wealth and treasure.

DURR-FULL:v2p393/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r12.claim: The Prophet describes the unpaid zakat as a bald snake that follows its owner and coils around his neck, then cites this verse.

DURR-FULL:v2p393/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r7.claim: The stingy people are People of the Book who concealed scripture instead of explaining it; 4:37 similarly describes their concealment and commands to conceal.

DURR-FULL:v2p393/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p393/r9.claim: They withheld spending in God's cause and failed to pay zakat.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r1.claim: The Prophet recites this verse as confirmation that withheld wealth becomes a bald, two-bumped snake which bites its owner's head through to the brain; another wording has it gnaw in the grave.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r2.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r2.claim: Unpaid wealth becomes a bald snake at resurrection and chases its owner as he flees.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r3.speaker: حجر بن بيان
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r3.claim: A relative who withholds God's bounty from kin will meet a lolling snake from Hell that coils around him; the report cites this verse.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r4.speaker: معاوية بن حيدة
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r4.claim: A man who refuses a dependent relative his surplus wealth will be summoned with a snake showing him the wealth he withheld.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r5.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله البجلي
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r5.claim: God brings a lolling snake from Hell to coil around one who withholds God's bounty from a relative who asks for it.

DURR-FULL:v2p394/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p394/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
